chapter: Mambo, the Palladium and Cubop City
title: Subway dances and the Blen Blen Club
summary: With Federico Pagani he handed out ten thousand flyers in subway stations, and with Chano Pozo's permission started the Blen Blen Club matinee with several bands.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I say: You want to work for us and for the Palladium? I say, okay, let's go out there; so we went out there, we went to the printer and we 10,000 throw-away and start to publicize the Wednesday night as a subway dance, And we had kids in all the subway stations in all New York giving away, five o'clock in the afternoon or five-thirty or six, all those people. The first ones that we had, the regular ones, there was thirty-five or forty or fifty people that used to go to the Palladium. The first ones that we publicized and we went to the radio, we had about 300, 480. The guy flipped. He said: "Gee, what is it"? and then Sunday was the same.

Forty people, from 2:00 o'clock in the afternoon to 2:00 o'clock in the night. Gee, it was terrible; so I said to the guy: You want to run the matinee the same way you run the Wednesday night? He says: "Machito, do whatever you please, we got to pay the rent, light and taxes, so please do whatever you want ." So Chano Pozo was alive and we went up there to the barrio, you know, to the neighborhood, and said: Chano, we need permission from you to use your name, the number "Blen, Blen" and we are going to call it "Blen, Blen" Club; so he give me a piece of paper giving me the permission to use it, the name "Blen, Blen" So we organized "Blen, Blen Club", without being recognized as incorporated in Albany. We had the permit from Chano Pozo.

We hired Noro Morales for one hour, We hired Jose Curbelo for one hour. We had the best around for one hour, so we had from 2:00 to 2:00. We had about five or six bands. Another success!! The first dance we had to check the coats down the ----, the place that was a Frank('s) restaurant, because they wasn't prepared to have seven or eight hundred people.
